newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher after weak correction.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher after weak correction.

text.p: COMEX copper settled higher as the market corrected slightly from the sharp losses of the previous two sessions.

Sentinment was helped early on by a drop of 1,325 tonnes in LME stocks to 269,825 tonnes. Trading was generally steadier and much less volatile, never straying beyond a cent-wide band after opening higher.
Traders expected some recovery after the steep losses on Wednesday and Thursday.
"The downside was excessive, therefore there was some shortcovering and profit-taking," said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities.

December COMEX ended 0.95 cent higher at 86.85 cents per pound, traded 87.50 to 86.50 cents. Spot September went out 1.05 cents firmer at 88.05 cents. Volume was estimated at 5,500 lots, well below Thursday's brisk 19,163 lots.
December ended the week just short of three cents weaker.
